title: Not All Evidence Is Admissible: Evidence Governance for Tool-Augmented Medical Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.22169v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Tool-augmented medical agents treat whatever their tools return as evidence. We show that this default is costly: medical tools fail silently, and a frozen reasoner cannot ignore what enters its context, so many cases it would have answered correctly are flipped to wrong once tool outputs are added. We call this evidence hijacking. $\mathcal{V}$-information explains the phenomenon: the reasoner has lost the option to ignore, so a tool output can carry negative usable information, and moving the decision of what to keep outside the reasoner restores that option. The theory further shows that part of any filtering gain comes merely from letting the reasoner see less, and only selection by content lets it see better. Building on this, we recast tool-augmented reasoning as evidence governance, which separates deciding what counts as evidence from the reasoner that answers, and propose context-independent evidence governance (CIEG), the first

translated_title: 并非所有证据都可采信：面向工具增强医疗智能体的证据治理
translated_abstract: 工具增强型医疗智能体通常将工具返回的任何内容都视为证据。我们证明这种默认做法代价高昂：医疗工具会无声地失效，而一个冻结（不可更新）的推理器无法忽略进入其上下文的内容，因此许多原本能够正确回答的案例，在加入工具输出后反而被翻转为错误答案。我们将这种现象称为“证据劫持”。V-信息理论可以解释这一现象：推理器已经失去了“忽略”的选项，因此工具输出可能携带负的可用信息，而将“保留什么”的决策移到推理器之外则可以恢复这一选项。该理论进一步表明，任何过滤带来的收益中有一部分仅仅来自于让推理器“看得更少”，而只有基于内容的筛选才能让推理器“看得更好”。基于此，我们将工具增强推理重新表述为证据治理，即把“什么算作证据”的决策与负责回答的推理器分离开来，并提出了上下文无关的证据治理方法（CIEG），这是首个……（摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该研究揭示了工具增强医疗智能体中的“证据劫持”现象——医疗工具无声失效会使原本正确的答案被翻转为错误——并从V-信息理论出发提出“证据治理”框架CIEG，通过将基于内容的证据筛选决策与推理器分离，使推理器不仅“看得更少”更能“看得更好”。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals "evidence hijacking" in tool-augmented medical agents—where silently failing tools flip originally correct answers to wrong—and, grounded in V-information theory, proposes context-independent evidence governance (CIEG), which separates content-based evidence selection from the frozen reasoner so it can not only see less but see better.
